_comment: Two entries. One refuses, one observes, and the difference decides everything about how
each is configured.
check-mode (preToolUse, Write) refuses a write the active mode, autonomy level or
three-strikes stop does not permit. failClosed is true, which is the standing rule for a
control. The blast radius is bounded on purpose: the matcher is Write, so if it ever
breaks, Shell still runs and the repository can be repaired from the terminal. A control
whose failure mode locks you out of fixing it is not a safety control.
record-attempt (postToolUse, Shell) writes down whether a test passed or failed. It never
denies — postToolUse cannot — and failClosed is false because there is nothing to fail
closed on: an observer that cannot read its input records nothing and blocks nothing. It
exists so the three-strikes stop is counted from what happened rather than from what the
agent says happened, which matters because the rule fires exactly when self-reporting is
worth least.
Both contracts were measured, not read: aios/bin/probe/results/hook-event-2026-08-01.md.
That file exists because M2-08 registered a hook against the documented contract and
blocked every shell command in the editor, twice. Two findings from it are load-bearing.
Cursor prefixes stdin with a UTF-8 BOM, which is almost certainly what that incident
recorded as 'empty stdin'. And postToolUse is the only event carrying an outcome, with
the exit code nested inside tool_output as a JSON string — and it is the shell's exit
code, not the command's, so record-attempt reads the runner's own verdict from the output
text instead.
deny-commands (preToolUse, Shell) is the third entry and the one M2-10 was raised to
finish. It refuses, and it is the one entry here with failClosed false. That is not an
oversight and it is the opposite of the standing rule, so the reason is on the record.
Its matcher is Shell: if it breaks there is no repair path through the terminal, because
the terminal is what it just took away. That was not reasoned about in advance, it was
measured — registering it with failClosed true and then leaving config.yml momentarily
half-written refused every command in the editor, and the only way back was the write
tool. The M2-08 outage, in the one place this file predicted it. Fail-closed is right for
the layer that is the containment; this layer is Advisory by ADR-012, so it does not buy
enough to be worth a repository nobody can fix. The script now allows and prints when it
cannot decide. A denial it can decide is still a denial.
It was run by hand against a real event, both shapes, before it was named here.
Q-005 — which interpreter a checked-in hook names — is not solved here, only survived.
`python` works on this machine and `python3` does not; neither is portable. ADR-006's
answer still stands: this becomes an aios subcommand and names no interpreter at all.
